§1.1 Existence of Atoms and Atomic Structure

1.1 Existence of Atoms and Atomic Structure

From Dalton’s Law of Definite Proportions and the Greek’s cutting argument, it becomes rather convincing that there is a small unit of matter. Given a microscope, Brownian motion further verifies the existence of such smallest unit of matter, define it as an atom.

Via radioactive material or Hydrogen gas in plasma phase, subatomic particles can be found to have charge and their charge-to-mass ratio may be determined through mass spectrometry. The Oil Drop Experiment [1] gives the charge. Hence, the mass is known. Rutherford’s experiment of bombarding gold foil with 𝛼 particles from RaBr2 then shows the existence of positively charged nuclei and its size relative to the atom. The size of an atom may be found through X-ray Crystallography, by diffraction to get the distance between two nuclei. The charge-to-mass ratio of an electron (or 𝛽 particle) then reveals the mass of the electron.

However, Newtonian mechanics would give the speed of the electron to be faster than light, which is impossible from Maxwell’s equations. The break-through point lies in the ultraviolet catastrophe motivates the postulate of quantized energy, which gives rise to planck’s constant. The same constant is then observed in the photoelectric effect as

𝐸=ℎ𝜈,(1.1.1)

and is verified by the fact that the excitation of the electrons dependent on the frequency but not intensity of the incident light. This assumption gives the particle-like description of light, the photon; however, Thomas Young showed in the Double Slit Experiment that light is also a particle. The particle light duality of light and the equation for its momentum 𝑝=𝐸𝜆 motivates the wave description for matter.
